definitionContent.para: A visual or aural presentation of system status, parameter values, or operational data to the flight crew. Indications are continuously or periodically displayed and do not require immediate crew action.

A notification to the flight crew that a system parameter has exceeded normal limits or a system fault has been detected. Alerts are classified as warnings, cautions, or advisories based on severity and required crew response time.

A text-based notification displayed on a multifunction display or Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System (EICAS) screen. Messages provide detailed information about system status, alerts, or crew procedures.

The highest level alert requiring immediate crew awareness and action. Warnings indicate conditions that could result in catastrophic failure, loss of aircraft control, or immediate danger to occupants. Typically displayed in RED with aural alert.

A medium-level alert requiring prompt crew awareness and action. Cautions indicate abnormal conditions that could degrade aircraft performance or result in system failure if not addressed. Typically displayed in AMBER/YELLOW with aural chime.

A low-level alert requiring crew awareness but not immediate action. Advisories provide information about system status changes or minor abnormalities. Typically displayed in CYAN or WHITE with no aural alert.

A centralized annunciation that one or more caution-level alerts are active. The master caution light illuminates AMBER and is located in a prominent position for immediate crew visibility. Pressing the master caution light acknowledges the alert.
A centralized annunciation that one or more warning-level alerts are active. The master warning light illuminates RED and is accompanied by continuous aural alert until acknowledged by the crew.

An electronic display that presents essential flight information including attitude, airspeed, altitude, heading, vertical speed, and flight director guidance. The PFD is the primary instrument for aircraft control.

An electronic display that presents navigation, system synoptic, engine parameters, and other secondary flight information. MFDs are configurable to show different pages based on flight phase and crew selection.

definitionSpec.definitionTerm: Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System (EICAS)

definitionContent.para: An integrated system that displays engine parameters, system status indications, and crew alerting messages. EICAS consolidates alerts from multiple aircraft systems into a prioritized message list.
An integrated monitoring and alerting system similar to EICAS, typically used in Airbus aircraft. ECAM provides system diagrams, corrective actions, and status information.
